memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Whatever the land yields during the sabbath year will be food for you
- for yourself, your male and female servants, and the hired worker and
temporary resident who live among you, as well as for your livestock and
the wild animals in your land. Whatever the land produces may be eaten'"
- Lev 25:5-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
During the Sabbath year the fields were not harvested in the usual way,
but whatever grew on its own could be eaten. And look carefully at who
was allowed to eat it: the landowner, yes, but also servants, hired
workers, temporary residents, livestock, and even wild animals.

In the ordinary years, the owner controlled the harvest. In the Sabbath
year, the fences came down. What grew freely was available freely, and
the poorest person had the same access as the richest.

Dear friend, this is a striking picture of God's heart. When human
systems of ownership were paused, God's default emerged — provision for
all, including the outsider and the animal.

We build careful walls around what is ours. God keeps gently asking us
to leave gaps in those walls for others to reach through. Earlier He told
Israel to leave the edges of their fields for the poor (Lev 23:22). Here
He opens the whole field for a year.

The early church caught something of this spirit. They shared what they
had so that there were no needy persons among them (Acts 4:34). Paul
wrote that the goal was equality, so that the one who gathered much did
not have too much, and the one who gathered little did not have too
little (2 Cor 8:14-15).

What wall around "mine" is God asking you to lower?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have I built walls around what is "mine"?
2. Who could benefit if I lowered them a little?
3. Does my generosity reach the outsider, or only my own circle?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You that Your heart is provision for all. Loosen my grip on
what I call mine, and make me generous toward those who have less. Amen.
